newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia palm olein stable in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia palm olein stable in late trade.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were generally stable in late trading on Monday, with crude palm oil finding few local buyers, traders said.

They said palm olein was quoted at 1,475-80 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, unchanged from the opening, but offers were also heard at 1,485 rupiah. Crude palm oil was on offer at 1,300 rupiah in the North Sumatran city of Medan, unchanged from the last done level, but there were no known takers.
"The market was rather quiet on a lack of demand," one trader said. "Buyers were also sidelined following the sharp falls in Malaysia as it might impact sentiment tomorrow."
Malaysian prices fell sharply on speculation the decrease in the country's February crude palm oil production could be smaller than initially anticipated by players.

The Malaysian Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) said over the weekend that January crude palm oil output fell by 9.57 percent to 576,967 tonnes from 638,045 tonnes in December, while end-January palm oil stocks fell to 696,272 tonnes from 794,454 at end-December.
"I don't understand why Malaysian prices are falling so sharply," one Indonesian trader said. "I believe it is the work of speculators."
